title: Regional adhesion and graceful eviction policy playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We need a repeatable, operational policy for multi-region request routing that balances latency SLOs, regional affinity (geo adhesion), and capacity-aware graceful eviction when regions are overloaded. Current behaviors either over-hedge (excess cross-region traffic raising cost and risk) or blindly reject/slow requests during regional pressure, causing customer-visible errors and violating P95 latency targets.

Goal: Define a routing playbook and implement runtime primitives to: (1) prefer local region with time-bound adhesion, (2) detect imminent capacity exhaustion early, (3) apply capacity-aware soft-eviction (percentage-based shed that preserves cache-locality-sensitive requests), and (4) incorporate circuit-breaker hysteresis to avoid oscillation and cascading failover. The policy must be measurable against SLOs and have clear rollback/canary steps.

Scope: In-scope: routing decision algorithm, admission/circuit-breaker thresholds, eviction prioritization rules (by tenant, request class, cache-sensitivity), telemetry to evaluate economic impact (tokens saved, latency delta), integration points with autoscaler and billing. Out-of-scope: model selection/quantization changes and long-term pricing model adjustments.

Constraints: Must not break existing API or customer routing pins; compatible with Dedicated and Private; minimal added tail latency (<5ms median decision time), observability hooks for per-tenant eviction metrics, and an operator-facing control plane toggle for immediate fallback to current routing behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A/B simulation shows ≤2% increase in P95 latency for non-evicted requests vs baseline under identical load
Under induced regional saturation tests, the policy keeps global error-rate increase <1% and reduces cross-region token spend by ≥15% compared to naive hedging
Telemetry surfaces per-tenant eviction counts, average time-in-adhesion, and capacity-credit balances in Console dashboard
Circuit breaker toggles fire, pause, and recover with documented hysteresis parameters (open/half-open/closed) and no oscillation in 60-minute golden-hour test
Playbook, rollout steps, and runbook included in Confluence and reviewed by PM and SRE
Feature gated behind runtime flag and can be disabled without restart; integration tests and chaos tests in CI pass

decisions: Prefer 'soft-eviction' (fractional shed) over binary deny for best-effort classes to preserve throughput while shedding load
Adopt 30s default adhesion window: after a client is routed cross-region for latency reasons it remains soft-pinned for 30s to preserve KV cache locality
Capacity model uses 'capacity credits' per region that decrement with accepted token work and replenish via autoscaler/steady-state credits; negative credits trigger eviction thresholds
Eviction priority: 1) best-effort anonymous traffic, 2) background embeddings, 3) on-demand low-priority tenants — preserve premium tenants and pinned routes when possible
Circuit breaker opens at sustained >85% consumed capacity-credits for 2m; half-open probes at 20% acceptance rate with exponential backoff for recovery testing
Fallback route order: local -> pinned-region -> geo-nearest healthy region -> global-fallback-model (lower-cost variant)
risks_mitigation: Risk: oscillation between regions during recovery — Mitigation: add global dampening window and require monotonic improvement before full re-adhesion
Risk: cache-locality loss increases token usage — Mitigation: adhesion windows and cache-sensitivity scoring to avoid evicting cache-beneficial traffic
Risk: misclassification of tenant priority — Mitigation: admin override and emergency pin feature; monitor for false positives and add telemetry alerts
Risk: operator error during rollout — Mitigation: runtime flag gating, staged canary (5% -> 25% -> 100%), and automated rollback on error-rate spike threshold

notes_for_oncall: If global error-rate increases >2% within 10m after rollout, flip runtime flag to disable feature and notify oncall lead

For customer escalations, use enterprise kill-switch to un-evict their traffic until root cause mitigated
When circuit breaker opens, do not manually route traffic without consulting infra lead; prefer increasing capacity or warming caches
